div.head: ECf 32 A 3
div.ab: Cum aliquid uero inopinatum uel dubium uel malum contra regnum uel contra coronam domini regis forte in balliuis suis subito emerserit, debent statim et incontinenti pulsatis campanis, quod Anglici uocant motbele, congregare et conuocare communas omnes et uniuersas, quod Anglici dicunt folkesmoth, scilicet uocatio et congregatio populorum et gentium omnium, quia ibi omnes conuenire debent et uniuersi, qui sub protectione et pace domini regis degunt et consistunt in regno predicto.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 655 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.

This passage is not part of ECf or ECf retr: it is one of the additions of the London collection (Leges Anglorum s. XIII in. Londoniis collectae), which Liebermann prints in smaller type across the page as an insertion into ECf retr. 32 (32 A–E, pp. 655–660). The dictionary cites it as “ECf 32 A …”, so it is kept with ECf here.
Liebermann’s letter a after “motbele” is his upright a (Erklärungen).

note.seg: dieser Traum vom Londoner Folcesmot als Reichscentrum, ohne dass König, Adel, Prälaten selbständig daneben treten, entsprang vielleicht aus Bestrebungen der City 1191 ff. Das husting i Lundene identificirt mit witene-imot auch Layamon v. 11542

this dream of the London folkmoot as the centre of the realm, without king, nobility or prelates standing independently beside it, perhaps arose from the aspirations of the City from 1191 on. Layamon v. 11542 too identifies the husting i Lundene with the witene-imot
